A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Liger research, with matching methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original benchmark evaluations, decoding latency and memory measurements, and component ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–E report original evaluations and ablations, including newly reported weight-change measurements and comparisons of gate construction sources.

M1.justification: The key-derived gates, softmax feature mapping, LoRA training objective, and hybrid recurrent/sliding-window architecture are retained. Section 3.3 newly specifies mixing weights alpha = beta = 0.5; v1 left these unspecified, so this documents implementation rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use cleaned Alpaca and evaluate PiQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, and MMLU, alongside the same decoding-length efficiency scenario. The added controls and analyses introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: GLA-3B is added to the scaling comparison in v2 Tables 4 and 11; v1 Tables 4 and 8 included GLA-1B but no GLA-3B. The principal SUPRA, LoLCATs, and Mamba2-Llama comparison sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new analyses introduce query/key/value pooling controls, ungated and recurrent-branch-removal controls, and absolute and normalized L1/L2 weight-change measurements. Existing benchmark metrics, training settings, and decoding procedures are retained; the newly specified mixing coefficients are implementation disclosure.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's gate-projection, feature-map, LoRA, and sliding-window ablations, v2 tests ungated linear attention and removal of the GLA branch in Tables 6 and 12. New Appendices C and D examine weight changes versus LoLCATs and query/key/value gate construction. These substantially expand investigation of component necessity, gate-source selection, and parameter preservation.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the statement that all experiments use random seed 0. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes LoLCATs-Llama-3-8B MMLU from 23.0 to 42.1 and its average from 62.2 to 65.4, substantially narrowing its reported gap to Liger, whose average changes from 67.0 to 67.6. New ablation, gate-source, GLA-3B, and weight-change results also appear. However, v2 Table 11 reports LoLCATs MMLU/average as 42.8/65.5, while Table 4 retains 62.2. These are definite reporting changes, with no documented setting changes explaining the conflicting retained-benchmark values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the gate parameterizations are retained. The new weight diagnostics and memory-indexing/MetaLA discussion provide empirical measures and conceptual motivation, without adding a formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the claims about reusing pretrained keys without additional gating parameters, hybrid Liger Attention, approximately 93% performance recovery at 0.02% of pretraining tokens, and applicability across 1B–8B models. Added supporting analyses do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 newly argues that mixing weights summing to one better approximate the original attention output distribution. Appendix C links smaller weight changes to reduced catastrophic forgetting, while Appendix D motivates key-derived gates through memory indexing and MetaLA's parameter-redundancy argument. These are new mechanism interpretations; no substantive new limitations are stated.

D1.justification: V2 discloses alpha = beta = 0.5 for hybrid attention and adds a model-collection access link alongside the existing code link. Hardware, optimizer, LoRA settings, batch configuration, training time, and memory disclosures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Based, Hymba, Titans, and Gershman et al.'s key-value memory work. Section 5 expands distinctions concerning local information, gating, and hybrid mixing, while Appendix D gives the already cited MetaLA additional motivational relevance. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include local language corrections, expanded hybrid-attention and related-work explanations, acknowledgements and author-role information, and new Appendices C–D preceding the relocated Full Results appendix.

P2.justification: The four figures are retained with limited caption editing. V2 adds Tables 7–8, expands the scaling and ablation tables, and reorders and redistributes the existing full-result tables as Tables 9–12. The visual design and table formats remain broadly stable.

improvement.justification: The added component and gate-source controls address gaps in v1's evidence, while explicit mixing weights and model-access information improve reproducibility. However, v2 introduces conflicting LoLCATs results across Tables 2, 4, and 11, weakening confidence in the central comparison. Appendix C also interprets weight norms as evidence of fewer changed parameters and reduced forgetting without directly testing those conclusions. These benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
